deep.reconstruction:
The page holds no derivations. It is a continuation of a table of quadratic residues for primes, carried over from folio 7v (443, 449, 457, 461, 463) and continued on 8v (491, 499, 503). For each prime p written in the margin (here 467, 479, 487), Gauss lists in increasing order every n with 1 <= n <= p-1 that is a square mod p, i.e. Legendre symbol (n/p) = +1.

The sign convention across folios 7v-8v is as follows (my reading, consistent with every entry I tested):
- For p ≡ 1 (mod 4), marked '∓' (449, 457, 461), -1 is a residue. The residue set is symmetric under n -> p-n, so only n <= (p-1)/2 is listed. For example, the 449 list stops at 224.
- For p ≡ 3 (mod 4), marked '+' (443, 463, and here 467, 479, 487), -1 is a non-residue. The set is not symmetric, so the full range up to p-1 is given, (p-1)/2 entries in all.

For 467 the list should have 233 entries, for 479 it should have 239, and for 487 it should have 243.

Each list starts as expected from quadratic reciprocity:
- 467 ≡ 3 (mod 8), so 2 is a non-residue. Also (3/467) = (7/467) = +1 and (5/467) = -1, giving 1, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 16, ...
- 479 ≡ 7 (mod 8), so 2, 3, 5 and 7 are residues and (13/479) = -1, giving 1, 2, ..., 12, 14, ...
- 487 ≡ 7 (mod 8), so 2 is a residue and 3, 5, 7 are non-residues, giving 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 15, 16, ...

For p ≡ 3 (mod 4) the tail mirrors the head with the character flipped. For 467 the list ends 461, 462, 465 (= -6, -5, -2) and omits 464 (= -3) and 466 (= -1).

The corrections visible on the page are consistent with genuine error-checking:
- In the 479 row, an entry after 233 at a line end is struck out. 234-239 are all non-residues mod 479, so the deletion is correct.
- Also in the 479 row, a blot between 362 and 363 is struck out.
- In the 487 row, a stretch between 303 and 311 and another between 315 and 322 are struck out. The numbers 297, 304, 307, 308 and 312 are written above the line as insertions. I checked: 297, 304, 307, 308, 311 and 312 are residues mod 487, while 305, 306, 309, 310 and 316-321 are non-residues. So the corrected row is right.

The page serves as a reference table: residue characters needed for class-number, cyclotomic or reciprocity computations, or for testing conjectures about the distribution of residues. Such tables were how Gauss's Disquisitiones-era empirical work was done.
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the many spot-checked entries. Among those checked were all of 220-224, 305-317, 389-394 and 461-466 mod 467; 51-55, 85-90, 185-192 and 234-239 mod 479; and 295-322, 452-453 mod 487.

The struck-out items (after 233 in the 479 row; between 303-311 and 315-322 in the 487 row) were Gauss's own erroneous entries. His deletions and the superscript insertions (297, 304, 307, 308, 312 for p=487) are correct.
I did not perform a full count of entries against (p-1)/2. Such a count, and a full set comparison, should be done by computer.

results.what: Complete lists of quadratic residues mod p for p = 467, 479, 487 (all p ≡ 3 mod 4, full range 1..p-1).
results.modern_name: Table of quadratic residues / Legendre symbol values
results.usually_credited_to: Tables of quadratic residues go back to Euler and Legendre. Gauss discusses and uses such tables in Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), Sect. IV.

results.what: Convention of listing only n <= (p-1)/2 for p ≡ 1 (mod 4) ('∓') but the full range for p ≡ 3 (mod 4) ('+'), exploiting the value of (-1/p).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine computational table of quadratic residues. Gauss is well known to have computed extensive residue tables. Nothing here goes beyond standard material he published or is known to have used.
